title: Computed Degraded-State Orchestrator — SLI Composition and Operator Runbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the Computed Degraded-State Orchestrator (DSO): a platform component and operator playbook that synthesizes multiple SLIs into a single, explainable degraded-state signal. The DSO provides a deterministic, actionable representation of platform health for operator workflows, automated fallback decisions, and dashboarding.

Background & motivation
-----------------------
- Problem: Individual SLIs (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, token-loss, queue-length, cost-per-token) are noisy and orthogonal. Operators frequently need a single semantic indicator (e.g., "degraded_network", "cache_stale", "compute_congestion") to decide safe mitigations.
- Goals:
  - Produce a computed degraded-state with clear composition rules and confidence score.
  - Make the signal auditable and reversible (operators can inspect contributing SLIs).
  - Drive automated routing/fallbacks and human runbook steps from the same signal.

Scope & non-goals
-----------------
- In scope: SLI composition rules for inference-serving platform, alert definitions, dashboard templates, operator runbook for triage and mitigation, testing and gameday checklist.
- Out of scope: model-level quality regressions (handled by the ML evals team), billing chargeback adjustments, and customer-facing incident comms templates.

Design: Computed Degraded-State (conceptual)
-------------------------------------------
1) Inputs (example SLIs):
   - request_success_rate (30s window)
   - p99_inference_latency_ms (1m window)
   - cpu_utilization_percent (per-pool, 30s)
   - gpu_memory_pressure_percent (per-device, 30s)
   - kv_prefix_cache_hit_rate (5m)
   - queued_requests_above_slo (rolling 1m)
   - token_spike_rate (tokens/s sustained over 1m)
2) Preprocessing: normalize each SLI to a [0..1] degradation score using directional bucketing and exponential smoothing (alpha=0.2 default).
3) Domain rules: map normalized scores to named sub-states using deterministic thresholds and a small rule engine (YAML rule list):
   - compute_congestion: p99_latency_score > 0.7 OR gpu_memory_pressure_score > 0.8
   - cache_stale: kv_hit_score > 0.6 AND queued_requests_score > 0.4
   - degradation_confidence: min(1, sum(weighted_scores) ) with configurable weights per team/workload.
4) Output: {state_name, confidence (0..1), top_contributors (3), timestamp, evidence_window}. (Note: in Confluence body we show JSON examples below.)

SLI composition rules (concrete examples)
---------------------------------------
- Normalization example: for a latency SLI where lower is better: normalized = clamp((value - good_threshold) / (bad_threshold - good_threshold), 0, 1).
  - good_threshold(p99) = 80 ms, bad_threshold(p99) = 400 ms.
- Weight defaults (global): p99_latency=0.4, error_rate=0.25, queue_depth=0.2, cache_hit=0.15. Teams may override weights per tenant policy.

Alerting & dashboards (operator-facing)
---------------------------------------
- Dashboard: "DSO — Regional Degraded-State" (per-region, per-pool): panels
  - computed_state timeline (stacked: normal, warning, degraded, critical)
  - top_contributors heatmap (last 30m)
  - SLI sparklines for the top 6 contributing metrics
  - recent automated actions (model swap, region-failover, tenant-eviction) with operator annotations

- Alerts (recommended):
  1) DSO.state >= degraded for > 2 minutes AND confidence >= 0.6 -> Notify oncall_platform (severity P2).
  2) DSO.state == critical OR any single SLI > 0.95 for 30s -> Trigger immediate paging (severity P1).
  3) DSO.confidence drift > 0.25 in 5m (high variance) -> Create a low-priority ticket for investigation.

Alert example (Prometheus-style pseudocode)
  - expr: max_over_time(dso_state_score{region="us-west-2"}[2m]) >= 0.6
  - labels: severity=P2, runbook_url=/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/dso-operator-runbook-2026

Operator runbook: triage and mitigation (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------------
1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
   - On page: Confirm alert scope: region/pool/tenant.
   - Run diagnostic query: dso_top_contributors(region, pool, window=10m).
   - Identify whether the top contributor is: compute_congestion, cache_stale, network_loss, or external-dependency.
2) Fast mitigations (5–20 minutes) — choose only one fast mitigation at a time and observe 2 min:
   - If compute_congestion: enable soft-eviction on low-priority tenants OR add burst capacity to the pool (if autoscaler allows).
     - CLI: redwoodctl pools burst-add --pool-id=pool-123 --tokens=50 --duration=10m
   - If cache_stale: trigger cache-prefetch for affected prefixes and prioritized tenants.
     - CLI: redwoodctl cache prefetch --prefix=sessions/tenant-42 --priority=high
   - If network_loss: reroute traffic to adjacent region fallback (if latency budget permits).
     - CLI: redwoodctl routing set-policy --region=us-west-2 --fallback=us-west-1 --apply
3) Deep mitigation (20–90 minutes)
   - If fast mitigations fail: initiate model-variant fallback to a smaller quantized variant (notify product owners).
     - Steps: Create rollout in Console: create rollout -> target pool -> model-variant=quantized-1 -> 25% canary -> monitor 10m -> roll to 100%.
   - If multi-region capacity shortage: coordinate cross-region failover with SRE (see cross-region-deploy-coordination playbook).
4) Post-incident actions (90+ minutes)
   - Record operator annotations: root-cause hypothesis, mitigations tried, time to initial mitigation, time to resolution.
   - Create follow-up ticket tagged dso:investigation for long-tail analysis.

Runbook decision matrix (compact table)
-------------------------------------
| Primary contributor | Fast mitigation | Escalation | Rollback condition |
|---------------------|-----------------|------------|--------------------|
| compute_congestion  | soft-evict low-priority | SRE (oncall) | p99_latency < 200ms for 10m |
| cache_stale         | prefetch prefixes | Platform infra | kv_hit_rate > 0.85 post-prefetch |
| network_loss        | reroute to fallback | Network team | packet_loss < 0.5% for 5m |

Automated action safety and manual gates
---------------------------------------
- Automated mitigations (soft-evict, model swap) are allowed with DSO.confidence >= 0.8 and a safety token check (operator approval token window disabled only for P1).
- Manual gates: Anything that changes customer-visible model quality (model-variant fallback) requires product-owner acknowledgement and a rollback playbook attached to the rollout.

Testing & gameday checklist (for platform owners)
------------------------------------------------
- Unit tests for normalization functions (edge cases: NaN, spikes, lost telemetry).
- Integration tests: Simulate compute congestion by injecting synthetic p99 latency (tool: dso-sim). Validations: computed_state transitions normal->warning->degraded->critical on expected thresholds.
- Gameday:
  1) Scenario: cache_stale across 3 pools. Operator must detect and prefetch within 10 minutes.
  2) Scenario: token_spike causing cascading queue growth. Validate automatic soft-eviction and model swap path.
  3) Post-gameday retro: update weights if DSO had false-positives > 2 in scoped exercises.

Metrics to monitor for DSO health
--------------------------------
- dso_state_transitions_total (by state)
- dso_confidence_histogram
- dso_false_positive_rate (per-sim) — measured in canary/validate runs
- dso_top_contributor_change_rate (frequency when top contributor changes)

Implementation notes & config snippets
-------------------------------------
- Rule YAML example (operator-editable):
  - name: compute_congestion
    expression: "p99_latency_score > 0.7 or gpu_memory_pressure_score > 0.8"
    weight: 0.4
    severity: degraded

- Normalization python snippet:
  def normalize_latency_ms(value, good=80, bad=400):
      if value <= good: return 0.0
      if value >= bad: return 1.0
      return (value - good) / (bad - good)

- Evidence payload (example JSON returned by DSO API):
  {
    "state": "degraded",
    "confidence": "0.72",
    "top_contributors": ["p99_latency", "gpu_memory_pressure"],
    "window": "2026-03-10T14:20:00Z/2026-03-10T14:30:00Z"
  }

Operational ownership & rollout plan
------------------------------------
- Owner: eng-platform (operator_experience squad) — primary oncall: platform-team-oncall.
- Phase 1 (2–4 weeks): deploy DSO read-only and dashboards, monitor false-positive rate using synthetic traffic.
- Phase 2 (4–8 weeks): enable low-impact automated mitigations (soft-evict) for low-priority tenants only; require operator approval token for higher-impact actions.
- Phase 3 (8–12 weeks): extend per-tenant weights and customer opt-out API; enable model-variant fallback as a guarded automated action with audits.

Postmortem & retrospective guidelines
------------------------------------
- Whenever DSO-triggered automation results in customer-visible impact: mandatory postmortem within 72 hours.
- Retro checklist for each incident: accuracy of top_contributors, time to mitigation, any conflicting downstream alarms, recommended rule/weight changes.

Appendix: quick queries and dashboard panels
-------------------------------------------
- Query: top contributors over 10m: topk(3, sum by(contributor) (increase(dso_contributor_score[10m])))
- Panel: "DSO Confidence by Pool" split by tenant-tier (line chart, 1m resolution)

------------------
